text: Understanding Git branching is an important skill for developers. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. When you start a new task, you create a feature branch, which keeps your changes separate and safe. Once your work is finished, you can merge the branch back into the main project. Many teams also use pull requests so that others can review the code before it is merged. This creates a clear version control workflow where everyone can track changes, avoid conflicts, and work together more efficiently. Learning to use branches well makes teamwork smoother and helps keep projects organized.
